**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use the checker-provided node roles**

For a fresh checker result containing a leaf `instruction_only` node—such as an unmarked instruction owner—this replaces the visually determined `node.role` with `score_owning` solely because the node has no descendants. The raw validator explicitly requires a role, but that evidence is discarded before comparisons and resolver packets are built, so `node_roles` and `mark_ownership` can be verified against a fabricated projection rather than the fresh visual read.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude superseded legacy checks from the resolver union**

When maker, fresh primary, and fresh second-read projections agree but either legacy projection differs, this union still includes the legacy-only disagreement and marks the row `resolver_required`. That contradicts the generated supersession receipt's claim that legacy checker authority is superseded and lets legacy output affect fresh-chain terminal states; compute the authoritative field union from the three fresh pairwise comparisons and retain legacy comparisons only for the supersession audit.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate checker raw responses during finalization**

If any of the 387 checker raw-response files is deleted, replaced, or moved after `prepare` succeeds, finalization still publishes a passing fresh-checker custody receipt because the authority assertion hashes only the stored ledger and binding claims, and `validateResolvers` subsequently materializes only resolver raw responses. Re-read every checker binding from the frozen pre-ledger/import here so the final evidence cannot certify checker bytes that are no longer present or hash-valid.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the repository head before passing the resume gate**

When this finalizer is run from a checkout whose `main` or predecessor head is not `e5e72baa...`, it still emits `status: 'pass'` and reports `exact_predecessor_main` because the value is only a hard-coded string; the script never reads or compares the relevant Git ref. Since this artifact is the safe-resume gate for subsequent batch work, check the actual ref before publishing a pass instead of merely recording the expected value.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require an explicit no-candidate-use attestation**

A raw checker response that sets `candidate_blind: true` but omits `candidate_responses_used` passes this condition because only the literal value `true` is rejected. In that scenario the repair certifies candidate blindness without the negative-use attestation the format otherwise records; require `candidate_responses_used === false` so missing or malformed values fail closed.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind each parsed resolver decision to its raw response**

When a resolver manifest pairs an accepted decision envelope with an unrelated raw-response file from the same resolver custody directory, this code validates both files' independent hashes but never proves that the parsed decision was derived from those raw bytes. Such a swapped or fabricated envelope can therefore enter the decision ledger while its cited raw authority says something different; parse and compare the raw response, or verify a parser-derived content hash, before accepting the decision.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate resolved field values before publishing them**

For any field decision whose `decision` is `resolved`, the candidate-value check is skipped and the arbitrary `result_value` is copied directly into the terminal projection. Because the only later projection check is self-equality with the resolver envelope, malformed owner paths, role tuples, mark values, or even wrong scalar types are accepted and published; validate every resolved value and the assembled projection against an explicit schema and cross-field invariants.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate every stored authority snapshot hash**

If one of the authority object's named snapshot fields—such as `pre_resolution_ledger_sha256` or `resolver_packet_set_sha256`—is altered while its stored `authority_sha256` is left unchanged, this assertion still succeeds because it compares only that aggregate string with the hash recomputed from current inputs. The final artifact then publishes snapshot hashes that are inconsistent with both its aggregate authority and the data; compare all recomputed snapshot fields or first recompute the aggregate from the authority object's own snapshots.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The 130 prior raws lacking the explicit attestation were superseded by fresh source-only visual reads, and the frozen role authority SHA is eb57ddab34241af9ebc2bf13900e2715722bf7cc55860110d818d8b7e3a4acb7.

Fixed at exact head c944cb30352d3f60c54a513a9cfb1f1d17425ce0. complete_disagreement_fields is now derived only from maker/fresh-primary, maker/fresh-second, and fresh-primary/fresh-second comparisons. Legacy comparisons remain in the additive supersession audit but cannot affect queue membership or terminal state. Fresh authority yields 62 agreements and 153 resolver decisions.

Fixed at exact head c944cb30352d3f60c54a513a9cfb1f1d17425ce0. Finalization now iterates all 387 rows in fresh-checker-import.v3.json and re-reads each raw path, byte length, and SHA inside its custody root before accepting any resolver output or publishing custody. The checked-in custody receipt conserves 217 primary plus 170 second reads.

Fixed at exact head c944cb30352d3f60c54a513a9cfb1f1d17425ce0. Finalization now resolves the actual origin/main ref, requires exact SHA e5e72baa24a7afb78075413673e0c25b0a37bc7c, and verifies it is an ancestor of HEAD before publishing the safe-resume gate.

body: Fixed at exact head c944cb30352d3f60c54a513a9cfb1f1d17425ce0. Candidate blindness now requires candidate_responses_used to exist as boolean false; missing, true, string, or other malformed values fail closed. Tests cover missing and string values. The 130 legacy raws that omitted the field were superseded and freshly rerun from source-only packets.

Fixed at exact head c944cb30352d3f60c54a513a9cfb1f1d17425ce0. Each resolver raw is re-read and normalized, then content-compared against its parsed envelope for question identity, packet SHA, complete field decisions, reasons/results, and resolved projection. All three producer dialects are additionally bound to exact terminal manifest, lock, and post-lock receipt hashes; 153/153 decisions pass.

Fixed at exact head c944cb30352d3f60c54a513a9cfb1f1d17425ce0. Every assembled projection, including arbitrary resolved values, now passes an explicit schema and cross-field validator covering exact shape, identities, pages, layout, ordered owner tuples, role/ownership consistency, printed-mark semantics, and evidence hashes. Validation runs before staging and again across all terminal resolved projections.

Fixed at exact head c944cb30352d3f60c54a513a9cfb1f1d17425ce0. assertPreResolutionAuthority now compares every field returned by createPreResolutionAuthority, including schema version, all four named snapshot hashes, and aggregate authority SHA. The mutation regression corrupts each stored field independently and requires fail-closed rejection.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Replace Map.groupBy for supported Node versions**

When this freeze command runs on the repository's supported Node 18/20 environments, execution reaches this line and throws `TypeError: Map.groupBy is not a function`; the repository declares Node >=18 and its workflows use Node 20, while this API is only available in newer releases. Consequently, the newly added authority-freeze script cannot reconstruct the checked-in rerun under the project's standard runtime.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Hash resolver assignments into the pre-resolution authority**

Include `packet_root` and `resolver_shard_assignments` in the authority hash rather than appending them after `createPreResolutionAuthority()` returns. If both external authority files are changed between preparation and finalization, `assertPreResolutionAuthority()` still passes because it recomputes only the ledger/packet/agreement/rejection snapshots, and the finalizer's equality check merely compares the two mutable copies; resolver worker assignments can therefore drift after the claimed freeze without detection.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject null marks on score-owning nodes**

When a resolver returns `node_roles: [['q01', 'score_owning']]`, matching `mark_ownership: [['q01', true]]`, and `printed_marks: [['q01', null]]`, this validation succeeds because only the `!owns` case constrains marks. That admits a terminal projection which violates the extraction schema's requirement that score-owning nodes have a nonnegative integer mark, allowing malformed resolver output into the verification ledger.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind resolver provenance to the raw response**

When a parser adds or changes `assigned_resolver_worker_id` or `source_read_attestation`, this raw-binding check still succeeds because it compares only the question, packet, projection, and field decisions. The finalizer subsequently validates the worker identity and merely requires a nonempty source attestation on the parsed decision, so provenance absent from—or different in—the hash-bound raw response can be injected during parsing and published as fresh resolver authority; compare these provenance fields against the normalized raw envelope as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refuse to freeze after terminal rerun outputs exist**

If stale or already-completed rerun outputs exist when `freeze` is invoked, this code still writes the authority with `frozen_before_terminal_raw_manifests: true` without checking the `rerun-outputs-v2` tree. The preparer later trusts this flag and accepts those terminal manifests, so the claimed pre-execution role freeze can actually be created after seeing the responses; fail closed when any terminal output already exists before recording this chronology assertion.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the rerun freezer into reconstruction provenance**

The candidate-attestation manifest, packet set, and source-role authority consumed by the preparer are generated by `issue_1666_freeze_candidate_rerun.mjs`, but the deterministic reconstruction receipt hashes only the finalizer, preparer, and validator. If the freezer changes, the receipt and checked-in manifest can remain valid while omitting the exact logic that selected and froze the rerun inputs, so the advertised reconstruction is incomplete; include the freezer path and hash in this component list.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject duplicate pages in resolved projections**

When a resolver emits a page chain such as `[2, 2]`, this validator accepts it because it checks only that every entry is a positive integer. The canonical extraction schema requires `complete_page_chain` items to be unique, so such a projection can be marked resolver-verified and enter the verification ledger even though it cannot form a valid downstream extraction; enforce uniqueness here before accepting the terminal projection.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve bundle custody paths before freezing packets**

When `source_bundle_path` contains `checker-bundles-v5/../...` or names a symlink inside that directory, this lexical `startsWith` check accepts a file outside the source-bundle custody root. Comparing its hash with the value declared by the same superseded raw response does not restore custody, so a candidate-bearing external file can be frozen into a packet advertised as source-only and candidate-blind; use canonical `realpath` containment before reading the bundle.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
